## Section: curriculum
```yml
heading: Course outline
items:
  - title: "Module 1 – Foundations of Clinical Pharmacology & Safe Prescribing"
    subtitle: "3 Days"
    module: module-1
    points: |
      - Day 1: Introduction to Clinical Pharmacology in Hospital Settings
      - Definition and scope of pharmacology
      - Drug classifications: OTC, prescription-only, controlled substances
      - Generic vs. brand names
      - Routes of administration (oral, IV, IM, subcutaneous, topical, etc.)
      - Overview of dosage forms and their implications in clinical settings
      - Day 2: Pharmacokinetics (ADME in the Hospital Setting) / Pharmacodynamics
      - Absorption: factors influencing oral drug absorption
      - Distribution: plasma protein binding, volume of distribution
      - Metabolism: hepatic pathways (CYP450), first-pass effect
      - Excretion: renal clearance, half-life, creatinine clearance
      - Mechanisms of action: receptor agonists/antagonists, enzyme inhibitors
      - Dose-response relationship
      - Therapeutic index and drug safety
      - Day 3: Prescription Writing and Interpretation
      - Components of a valid prescription
      - Standard abbreviations and those to avoid
      - Legal and regulatory considerations
      - Time-critical medications
  - title: "Module 2 – Therapeutics in Acute & Chronic Care"
    subtitle: "3 Days"
    module: module-2
    points: |
      - Day 4: Practical Use of Antimicrobials in Hospitals
      - Classification and mechanisms of common antibiotics
      - Empirical vs. targeted therapy
      - Duration of treatment and de-escalation
      - Antibiotic resistance mechanisms
      - Local antibiogram use
      - Day 5: Cardiovascular Drugs in Acute and Chronic Care
      - Antihypertensives: ACE inhibitors, beta-blockers, calcium channel blockers
      - Diuretics: loop, thiazide, potassium-sparing
      - Emergency drugs: nitrates, atropine, adenosine
      - Monitoring: BP, electrolytes, ECG
      - Day 6: Pain Management and Analgesic Use
      - WHO analgesic ladder
      - Non-opioids: paracetamol, NSAIDs
      - Opioids: morphine, fentanyl, tramadol
      - Patient-controlled analgesia (PCA)
      - Opioid-induced respiratory depression
  - title: "Module 3 – Special Populations, Critical Care & Emergency Pharmacology"
    subtitle: "3 Days"
    module: module-3
    points: |
      - Day 7: Drug Dosing in Renal and Hepatic Impairment / Pharmacology in Special Populations
      - Creatinine clearance estimation (Cockcroft-Gault)
      - Hepatic function indicators (AST, ALT, INR)
      - Dose adjustment examples: aminoglycosides, metformin
      - Hepatotoxic and nephrotoxic drugs
      - Geriatric considerations: polypharmacy, altered metabolism
      - Pregnancy categories and breastfeeding safety
      - Day 8: Emergency Medications and Crash Carts
      - ACLS drugs: adrenaline, amiodarone, atropine, naloxone
      - Dosing and routes (IV push, IM, intraosseous)
      - Crash cart organization and access
      - Drug stability and reconstitution
      - Day 9: Pharmacology in ICU and Critical Care
      - Sedatives: midazolam, propofol
      - Vasopressors: norepinephrine, dopamine
      - Neuromuscular blockers
      - Therapeutic Drug Monitoring (TDM)
  - title: "Module 4 – IV Therapy, Medication Safety & Clinical Integration"
    subtitle: "3 Days"
    module: module-4
    points: |
      - Day 10: IV Fluids, Drips, and Infusion Calculations
      - Types of IV fluids: isotonic, hypertonic, hypotonic
      - Compatibility and stability of IV meds
      - Calculating drip rates and flow rates
      - Common IV meds: insulin, heparin, dopamine
      - Day 11: Medication Safety and Error Prevention / Interprofessional Roles in Medication Safety
      - Types of errors: prescribing, transcribing, dispensing, administration
      - High-risk medications (LASA drugs)
      - Safety practices: tall man lettering, double-checks
      - Reporting systems and culture of safety
      - Medication reconciliation
      - Drug rounds and interdisciplinary huddles
      - ADR, Med Error reporting and near-miss documentation
      - Day 12: Assessment, Integration & Multidisciplinary Review
      - Quiz (MCQs, Case Studies, calculations, drug matching)
      - OSCE-style practical stations (e.g., interpreting a drug chart, calculating infusion, identifying errors)
      - Group presentations of case studies
      - Feedback collection
```
